In mathematics, '''Brandt matrices''' are [[matrix (mathematics)|matrices]], introduced by {{harvs|txt|authorlink=Heinrich Brandt|last=Brandt|year=1943}}, that are related to the number of [[ideal (ring theory)|ideals]] of given norm in an ideal class of a definite [[quaternion algebra]] over the [[rational number|rationals]], and that give a representation of the [[Hecke algebra]].

{{harvtxt|Eichler|1955}} calculated the traces of the Brandt matrices.

Let ''O'' be an [[Order (ring theory)|order]] in a quaternion algebra with [[Class number (number theory)|class number]] ''H'', and ''I''<sub>i</sub>,...,''I''<sub>''H''</sub> invertible left ''O''-ideals representing the classes.  Fix an integer ''m''.  Let ''e''<sub>''j''</sub> denote the number of units in the right order of ''I''<sub>''j''</sub> and let ''B''<sub>''ij''</sub> denote the number of α in ''I''<sub>''j''</sub><sup>−1</sup>''I''<sub>''i''</sub> with [[reduced norm]] N(α) equal to ''m''N(''I''<sub>''i''</sub>)/N(''I''<sub>''j''</sub>). The Brandt matrix ''B''(''m'') is the ''H''×''H'' matrix with entries ''B''<sub>''ij''</sub>.  Up to conjugation by a [[permutation matrix]] it is independent of the choice of representatives ''I''<sub>''j''</sub>; it is dependent only on the level of the order ''O''.
